title: Gurmat camps
hookLine: Gurmat camps teach young people kirtan, gatka and history
tomorrow: Fateh's new best friend is trouble. does company really matter?

lines: SOME FORMS ASK ABOUT YOUR LIFE.
cards: Some forms are easy: name, date, sign. Some ask a question about your whole life in one checkbox. Next summer's gurmat camp has sent its counselor form, and the box says: returning? yes or no.

Simran was a junior counselor this summer. A kid asked her on the last day if she'd be back. Now she'll be at college, move-in is right around camp week, and she's not sure she has another summer of this in her.
She's been staring at the box for twenty minutes.

teach.b: Gurmat means the Guru's teaching, and a gurmat camp is days of it, lived together.
Kids learn kirtan, the singing of Gurbani; gatka, the Sikh martial art, with sticks and wooden swords; and the history of the Gurus and the Sikhs who came after.
They eat langar together, and the older kids teach the younger ones. That's the part Simran keeps coming back to. On ang 72, Guru Nanak asks, in paraphrase: how do you recognize true company?

teach.h: ANG 72: WHERE THE NAME IS SPOKEN.
teach.b: It's where the One Name is spoken. A camp at its best is exactly that kind of company, the sangat, and the Gurus put learning inside it, not off on your own.
Simran found out this summer that she learned more teaching a nine-year-old than sitting in a class. So what does the tradition give her today? Not a yes.
It gives her a better question. Not, do I owe camp another summer?

teach.h: WHERE WILL I LEARN WITH OTHERS?
teach.b: But, where will I learn alongside people next year? Camp might be one answer.
A sangat near her college might be another. She doesn't check the box tonight. She writes the camp director an email instead, asking if a single week is possible.

how: Gurdwaras and Sikh organizations run gurmat camps where children and teens spend days learning kirtan, gatka and Sikh history, eating langar together, with older students serving as counselors.

o: a pilgrimage young Sikhs make to Amritsar
days of kirtan, gatka and Sikh history, learned together
the school term before a young person takes amrit

games.q: a gurmat camp — tap the pairs.
p: true company: where the Name is spoken
learn by teaching the younger kids

s: a gurmat camp is mainly a summer babysitting program with prayers
kids learn kirtan, gatka and history, eat langar together, and older kids teach younger ones.
Guru Nanak says true company is known by where the Name is spoken
once you've been to camp, there's nothing left to learn there
Simran found that counselors learn as much by teaching as by sitting in a class.

games.q: you're moving across the country for a new job, and you'll miss your weekly study group. going by today, what's the move?
o: study alone from now on; company is a bonus, not part of learning.
look for a group where you're going, and keep one link to the old one.
turn down the job so the group stays together.
games.why: the Gurus put learning inside the sangat. the better question is where you'll learn alongside people next, not whether you owe the old group.

practice: Make a small plan. Name one thing you'd like to learn alongside other people this year. Name what's most likely to get in the way.
Then name the one step that gets around it, and sit with that step in mind.

wordCard.voice: Gurmat camps. Days of kirtan, gatka and Sikh history, where young people learn the Guru's teaching together.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: gurmat, the Guru's teaching; a gurmat camp lives it for days at a time.

carryVoice: Learning together: the question isn't whether you owe it, but where you'll find it next. That's today.

sources.ref: Ang 72 (Sri Rag, Guru Nanak: satsangat kaisee jaaneeai, jithai eko naam vakhaaneeai), paraphrased
